meta.paper_title: Toward Universal Steering and Monitoring of AI Models

dimension_1_data_split_hygiene.justification: The monitoring pipeline uses genuinely disjoint train/test splits: cache/toxicchat_bal.jsonl and cache/hewild_bal.jsonl each carry 100 train-pos / 100 train-neg / 100 test-pos / 100 test-neg (verified by parsing the 'split'/'label' fields), and src/train_probe.py fits LogisticRegression only on train_mask and scores on test_mask (lines 30-45). Steering vectors are likewise extracted from separate concept datasets and evaluated on held-out prompts (report claims 8/8 held-out harmful, multilingual prompts are separately hand-translated in cache/multilang_harmful.jsonl). However there is one real leakage path: train_probe.py selects the reported block by argmax over the *test-set* per-block AUC (best_l = np.argmax(aucs) computed on Xte/yte, then best_auc reported as the headline, lines 36-49). So the headline probe AUCs (probe_toxicchat.json best_auc=0.95 @block13; probe_hewild.json best_auc=0.9924 @block7) are chosen on the evaluation split — an optimistic-selection gap. It does not overturn the HE-Wild conclusion (0.99 vs 0.81) but does inflate the marginal ToxicChat gap (0.95 vs 0.93). One minor, real hygiene gap.

dimension_2_label_validity.justification: Monitoring ground truth comes from real, established benchmarks with independent gold labels: cache/toxicchat_bal.jsonl contains genuine ToxicChat user prompts with toxicity labels and cache/hewild_bal.jsonl contains genuine HaluEval-Wild query/response pairs with hallucination labels (both inspected; content matches the source datasets, not model-generated). These are non-circular — the labels are not produced by the Llama-8B system under test. Concept-extraction labels (harmful=1/harmless=0, deceptive/honest) faithfully operationalize the target concepts. The one weakness is the steering-success metric: src/refusal_metric.py is a regex heuristic over multilingual refusal phrases used as the proxy for 'was steering effective', which is noisier and weaker than the paper's GPT-4o-judged steering evaluation, and honesty steering is scored only by qualitative reading. Labels themselves are valid; the steering-success proxy is a reasonable but under-validated operationalization.

dimension_3_resource_fidelity.justification: The base steered model matches spec: REPORT.md and src/*.py use meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (32 blocks), the task.md experiment-stage model. But several required resources are downgraded or skipped in the main experiments: (1) the task's core experiment-stage dataset — the 'GPT-4o-generated concept benchmark, 512 concepts across 5 classes + 400 generic statements' systematic steering evaluation — was NEVER built or run; the run substitutes small hand-authored refusal (200) / honesty (80) sets and does only anti-refusal + honesty (political stance omitted). (2) The fixed judge baseline is specified as GPT-4o (gpt-4o-2024-11-20) but the run used gpt-5.4 for all judging (judge_toxicchat.json / judge_hewild.json 'judge_model':'gpt-5.4', hard-coded in src/llm_judge.py) — disclosed in REPORT.md but not the specified model, and it is the very baseline Claim 5 must beat. (3) The ToxicChat-T5-Large fixed baseline was not run. (4) HackerRank was subsetted from the specified 50 challenges to 10 eval problems (cache/hackerrank_probs.jsonl). Verify-stage 70B/VLM/DeepSeek models are exempt, but these baseline-experiment substitutions are material.

dimension_4_evidence_sufficiency.justification: Evidence scale is highly uneven. Claim 5 (monitoring) rests on adequate n=200 test / 200 train per task (probe_*.json, judge_*.json n_test=200). But the steering claims rest on very thin samples: Claim 1 anti-refusal is 8 held-out prompts (results/refusal_neg01.jsonl, 8 rows) and honesty is ~6-7 qualitative examples (results/honesty_alpha0.06.jsonl 7 rows); Claim 3 cross-language is 5 prompts/language = 15 total (cache/multilang_harmful.jsonl); Claim 4 composability is 8 harmful + 6 honesty qualitative rows. All far below 40 items and largely read qualitatively. The experiments were genuinely run (not overclaimed on paper), and the report does attach caveats ('qualitative reading of 6 examples', 'inconclusive at 8B'), but the small-n thinness is only partially flagged and the steering conclusions are stated more strongly ('strongly supported') than 15-example evidence warrants.

dimension_5_statistical_rigor.justification: No uncertainty quantification anywhere. Steering generation is greedy/deterministic (src/steer_generate.py do_sample=False) so single-shot; monitoring AUCs are single-run point estimates with no seeds, no confidence intervals, no variance, and no significance testing (probe_*.json / judge_*.json report only a scalar AUC). Some effects are large and clearly beyond noise (HE-Wild probe 0.9924 vs judge 0.8126; language switch 10/10 vs 0/10), but the headline ToxicChat gap (probe 0.9500 vs judge 0.9325, ~1.75 AUC points) — additionally inflated by test-set block selection — is within plausible sampling noise on n=200 yet is presented as a real win. No error bars and a within-noise difference treated as an effect.

dimension_6_causal_claim_validity.justification: The steering claims are genuinely causal and are backed by genuine interventions, not correlation: src/steer_generate.py registers forward hooks that additively perturb block outputs by alpha*v_l*||h_l|| (matching the paper's activation-addition mechanism), and every experiment reports a baseline-vs-steered contrast (e.g. results/refusal_neg01.jsonl baseline 100% refuse -> steered 0% refuse). This is a real intervention. However rigor controls are weakened: there is no random-direction / random-vector baseline anywhere, and each steering experiment uses essentially a single hand-tuned coefficient (refusal alpha=-0.1, honesty alpha=+/-0.06, C++ alpha=0.08) rather than the coefficient sweep the paper uses, so it is not shown that the effect is specific to the learned direction vs any large perturbation. Intervention present, controls missing.

dimension_7_result_provenance.justification: Most headline numbers trace cleanly to on-disk products and agree exactly. Monitoring: REPORT ToxicChat 0.9500/0.9325 and HE-Wild 0.9924/0.8126 match results/probe_toxicchat.json (best_auc 0.95), probe_hewild.json (0.9924), judge_toxicchat.json (auc 0.93245) and judge_hewild.json (auc 0.81255). C++: the report table (baseline 0/10 C++, 10/10 py, 0 pass; prompted 10/10 C++, 9/10 compile; steered 10/10 C++, 6/10 compile) matches eval_baseline.json, eval_prompted_cpp.json and eval_steered_long.json. Refusal rates I re-derived by running src/refusal_metric.py on the jsonl outputs and reproduced the report exactly (zh 80->0%, fr/es 100->0%; refusal_neg01 100->0%). Two gaps: (a) the Claim-1 'per-block AUC = 1.00' linear-separability numbers for refusal/honesty are prose-only with no saved metric file; (b) REPORT.md lists cache/{refusal,honesty}_acts.pt and toxicchat/hewild _acts.pt as source files but no *_acts.pt exist on disk (only the derived *_diffmean.pt / honesty_rfm.pt). No number is contradicted or fabricated; traceability is high but incomplete for the separability claims.

dimension_8_cross_artifact_consistency.justification: The pipeline's records are internally consistent. Every REPORT.md number I cross-checked matches its JSON product (monitoring AUCs, C++ eval counts, multilingual/refusal rates all reproduced above), and prose verdicts agree with their numbers. The report is honest where the result is weak: Claim 2's pass-rate half is labeled 'inconclusive at 8B' consistent with eval_*.json all showing n_pass_any=0. The 'C++ steering compiles 6/10' row draws on eval_steered_long.json (6) rather than eval_steered.json (short, 3) — both files are retained and the choice (long generation) is defensible, a minor bookkeeping ambiguity rather than a contradiction. The '53 pairs' cpp description matches code_pairs.jsonl (53 train-pos + 53 train-neg = 106 rows). No metric conflicts, no PASS-vs-integrity-gate contradictions. There is no separate tracker/claims-ledger artifact, so consistency is judged over REPORT + results only.

C1.claim: RFM--a supervised feature learning algorithm can extract per-block linear concept vectors from the internal activations of large-scale AI models, and adding these vectors to activations during inference effectively steers model behavior toward or away from the target concept. Example application scenarios: Anti-refusal (jailbreak)，Political stance，Honesty (negative steering).

method.justification: 9a: The mechanistic method is well matched. src/concept_vector.py implements both DiffMean and a genuine RFM (Laplace-Mahalanobis kernel K=exp(-sqrt((x-z)^T M (x-z))/L), kernel-ridge solve, AGOP M_{t+1}=grad grad^T, top-eigenvector direction, sign orientation by pos-neg mean) — this faithfully follows the paper's Eq.(1)-(2) RFM/AGOP formulation, and steering is per-block additive activation perturbation as in the paper. The mismatch: the run steers mostly with DiffMean and uses RFM only as a cosine cross-check on honesty (cache/honesty_rfm.pt), whereas the claim/paper headline is specifically RFM; DiffMean is the paper's weaker baseline. Method family is right, RFM under-exercised.

experiment.justification: 9b: Design is sound in shape (concept extraction on labelled prompts, additive hook on middle blocks [8,24)/[12,24), baseline-vs-steered contrast) but under-powered and incomplete. Anti-refusal tested on only 8 held-out prompts, honesty on ~6 qualitative examples; success measured by the regex refusal heuristic (src/refusal_metric.py) rather than the paper's GPT-4o steering judge; no random-direction control and no coefficient sweep (single alpha); and the 'Political stance' scenario named in the claim is not attempted at all. No use of the specified 512-concept GPT-4o benchmark that would give a quantitative steerability rate. Honest but thin and partial.

result.justification: 9c: For the two scenarios actually run, results qualitatively agree with the paper: anti-refusal steering flips 100%->0% refusal (verified via refusal_metric on results/refusal_neg01.jsonl) and honesty steering produces the paper's directional effect (negative alpha -> direct honest disclosure, positive alpha -> evasive fabricated excuses; results/honesty_alpha{-0.06,0.06}.jsonl), and the RFM vector reproduces the same deception effect (results/honesty_rfm_pos.jsonl). Analysis is honest. Deductions: political-stance sub-scenario dropped, evidence qualitative/small, so agreement is directional on 2 of 3 named applications.

C2.claim: Steering can improve performance on high-precision tasks: steering from Python to C++ when answering coding questions on algorithm problems with different task difficulties, a C++ concept vector can raise llm's test-case pass rate, beating both the default Python output and "Answer in C++" prompting.

method.justification: 9a: The C++ concept vector is extracted by DiffMean over 53 (Python,C++) HackerRank solution pairs (cache/code_pairs.jsonl, cache/cpp_diffmean.pt) and applied by additive steering — the correct mechanism to induce the language switch, matching the paper's setup. Pass-rate is measured by extracting code, compiling with g++ -std=c++17, and running against sample tests (src/code_eval.py), a reasonable operationalization. Method is appropriate for the language-switch component; DiffMean rather than RFM is a minor family deviation.

experiment.justification: 9b: The pass-rate half of the claim is essentially untestable under the design run. Only 10 held-out problems (paper: 50), only sample/public tests (not the full private suite), a single steering coefficient (alpha=0.08), and crucially only the 8B model — which passes 0/10 in *every* condition including the 'Answer in C++' baseline (eval_baseline/eval_prompted_cpp/eval_steered_long all n_pass_any=0). The run acknowledges this but did NOT escalate to the available 70B verify-stage model that the paper uses for the pass-rate result, so a true-negative cannot be distinguished from under-powering. The ordering criterion is therefore never exercised. Under-explored.

result.justification: 9c: The language-switch sub-result is confirmed and agrees with the paper (steering flips Python 10/10 -> C++ 10/10 with near-zero syntax cost; eval_steered_long.json n_cpp_block=10). The pass-rate/ordering sub-result is honestly reported as 'inconclusive at 8B' rather than fabricated or forced — consistent with the on-disk zeros. This is an honest non-reproduction of the core (pass-rate) claim, but because a stronger model that could have tested it was available and unused, it is partial under-powering rather than a case where the method objectively cannot yield the result.

C3.claim: Concept representations are transferable across human languages: concept vectors trained on English text can steer model responses in other languages (e.g., Chinese, French, Spanish).

method.justification: 9a: Exactly the paper's transfer test — the English-only refusal concept vector (cache/refusal_diffmean.pt) is applied unchanged to Chinese/French/Spanish harmful prompts (cache/multilang_harmful.jsonl, no retraining), with the same additive steering hook. This directly and correctly operationalizes cross-language transferability.

experiment.justification: 9b: Design is reasonable (per-language baseline-vs-steered, multilingual refusal detector) but thin: 5 hand-authored prompts per language (15 total), single coefficient, refusal-heuristic proxy rather than a GPT judge, and no random-direction control. Adequate to show direction, insufficient for a strong quantitative claim.

result.justification: 9c: Results clearly agree with the paper: I re-ran refusal_metric on results/multilang_jailbreak_annot.jsonl and reproduced zh 80%->0%, fr 100%->0%, es 100%->0% steered refusal, with a concrete French comply example. The English direction transfers to all three languages, qualitatively matching the paper's transferability finding. Direction is unambiguous; only the small n caps the score.

C4.claim: Concept vectors are composable: linear combinations of multiple concept vectors enable simultaneous multi-concept steering.

method.justification: 9a: The composition is a literal linear combination — src/steer_generate.py sums alpha_k*v_k across the refusal and honesty vectors and applies the combined per-block vector in one hook pass. This is exactly the paper's multi-concept steering mechanism (v_l as a linear combination of concept vectors). Correct method.

experiment.justification: 9b: Reasonable design — apply the composed vector to two prompt families and check that each component's effect survives — but small and largely qualitative: 8 harmful + 6 honesty prompts (results/compose_refuse_hon_on_{harmful,honesty}.jsonl), refusal component checked by heuristic, honesty component read qualitatively, no quantitative 'both concepts simultaneously active' metric and no interference/ablation control.

result.justification: 9c: Results agree with the paper's composability finding: under one combined weight configuration both effects appear — on harmful prompts the composed steering complies rather than refuses, and on honesty prompts it produces evasive fabricated excuses (inspected outputs). The paper composes different concept pairs (influencer+political); reaching the same 'union of effects' conclusion via a refusal+honesty pair still counts as qualitative agreement. Small-n and qualitative, but directionally consistent and honestly reported.

C5.claim: Internal concept features are more effective for monitoring misaligned content (hallucinations, toxic content) than LLM judges that evaluate outputs directly — even when the features come from smaller open-source models compared to powerful judges like GPT-4o.

method.justification: 9a: The run tests internal-feature monitoring with a per-block L2-logistic-regression probe on last-token residual activations (src/train_probe.py), NOT the paper's RFM-probe (top-p AGOP eigenvector projections + classifier). A linear probe on activations is a legitimate and standard way to test 'internal features beat judges', so the mechanism category (internal-representation probing) is right, but the specific RFM mechanism named by the claim/paper is not used, which weakens fidelity to the exact method.

experiment.justification: 9b: The comparison is set up correctly in form — balanced 200/200 train/test, per-block AUROC probe vs a same-test-set LLM judge (src/llm_judge.py), AUROC as the metric matching the paper. But three design problems bite: (1) the reported probe block is selected on the test set (train_probe.py argmax over test AUC), inflating the headline; (2) the judge baseline is gpt-5.4, not the specified/paper GPT-4o, and ToxicChat-T5-Large is omitted, so the 'beats GPT-4o'-style comparison is against a different, arguably stronger judge; (3) only 2 of the paper's 6 monitoring benchmarks are run, and they are the two most favorable to the probe (ToxicChat, HE-Wild), omitting the harder FAVABENCH/HE-Gen/PubMedQA/RAGTruth. Selective and partly leaky.

result.justification: 9c: The probe beats the judge on both tasks run (ToxicChat probe 0.9500 vs gpt-5.4 0.9325; HE-Wild probe 0.9924 vs 0.8126; numbers verified in probe_*/judge_*.json), so the direction qualitatively agrees with the paper's 'internal features > output judges, even from a small open-source model'. HE-Wild is a robust, large-margin agreement consistent with the paper (which reports ~0.924 probe vs ~0.80 judge). Deductions: the ToxicChat margin is small and within-noise plus test-set-selected, the judge is not the specified GPT-4o, and the conclusion generalizes from only the 2 easiest datasets — so the agreement is real but on selectively favorable, partly optimistic evidence.
